title: Adding arrows to ggswim
text: demonstrate might add arrows onto patient_data dataset, let’s take subset patient_data help us make use geom_swim_arrow(): dataset derived patient_data joined end-study labels. Since populated labels end_study_events mean subject went study, arrows applicable subjects end-study status. Now let’s use geom_swim_arrow() combination geom_swim_lane() make swimmer plot:  ’ve assigned arrows subset patients met end--study event. Note geom_swim_arrow() gives control arrow head, neck, colour/color, shape, length. geom_swim_arrow() also allows aesthetically mapped x start xend values. prefer arrow neck lengths come data, supply x xend aes().
code: library(ggswim) library(ggplot2)  arrow_data <- patient_data |>   dplyr::left_join(     end_study_events |>       dplyr::select(pt_id, label),     by = "pt_id"   ) |>   dplyr::select(pt_id, end_time, label) |>   dplyr::filter(.by = pt_id, end_time == max(end_time)) |>   dplyr::filter(is.na(label)) |>   unique()  arrow_data #> # A tibble: 8 × 3 #>   pt_id end_time label #>   <chr>    <dbl> <chr> #> 1 04         9   NA    #> 2 09        12   NA    #> 3 13         2.5 NA    #> 4 14         0.9 NA    #> 5 15         0.9 NA    #> 6 17         2.8 NA    #> 7 18         3.3 NA    #> 8 19         6   NA patient_data |>   ggplot() +   geom_swim_lane(     mapping = aes(       x = start_time, xend = end_time, y = pt_id,       color = disease_assessment     ),     linewidth = 5   ) +   geom_swim_arrow(     data = arrow_data,     mapping = aes(xend = end_time, y = pt_id),     arrow_neck_length = 5,     arrow_head_length = grid::unit(0.15, "inches"),     arrow_colour = "firebrick",     arrow_fill = "gold"   )

title: Adding arrows to ggswim
text: addition specifying arrow appearance directly parameters, arrows can also styled using arrow aesthetic together scale_arrow_discrete(). approach allows arrow styles controlled ggplot2 scaling system, making easier add arrows legend component manage multiple arrow styles. demonstrate approach, can map value arrow aesthetic define appearance using scale_arrow_discrete():  , “Continuation” value mapped arrow aesthetic used scale_arrow_discrete() determine arrow’s visual properties. mapping treated like discrete scale ggplot2, can also displayed separate legend entry desired. Using scale_arrow_discrete() particularly helpful : arrows appear dedicated legend component multiple arrow styles required arrow styling managed consistently across plots simple cases, specifying arrow parameters directly geom_swim_arrow() may still sufficient. However, using scale_arrow_discrete() provides flexible scalable approach working complex swimmer plots.
code: patient_data |>   ggplot() +   geom_swim_lane(     mapping = aes(       x = start_time, xend = end_time, y = pt_id,       color = disease_assessment     ),     linewidth = 5   ) +   geom_swim_arrow(     data = arrow_data,     mapping = aes(       xend = end_time,       y = pt_id,       arrow = "Continuation"     ),     arrow_neck_length = 5,     arrow_head_length = grid::unit(0.15, "inches")   ) +   scale_arrow_discrete(     limits = "Continuation",     colours = "firebrick",     fills = "gold",     types = "closed",     name = NULL   )

title: Adding arrows to ggswim
text: Arrow layers inherit plot data aesthetics just like ggplot2 layers. supplying separate arrow dataset, use inherit.aes = FALSE lacks variables used global mappings, map y xend explicitly (x specifying endpoints). example, plot global colour mapping present arrow_data, turn inheritance arrow layer:  custom arrow styles, supply event categories limits order colours, fills, types. Vector names control matching. default arrow palette supplies one style; multiple categories need explicit styles limits. Use separate layers combining open closed arrows one panel. Standard colour settings overridden arrow styling; use arrow_colour fixed styling arrow aesthetic scale matching legend.
code: ggplot2::ggplot(patient_data, ggplot2::aes(colour = disease_assessment)) +   geom_swim_lane(ggplot2::aes(x = start_time, xend = end_time, y = pt_id)) +   geom_swim_arrow(     data = arrow_data,     mapping = ggplot2::aes(xend = end_time, y = pt_id),     inherit.aes = FALSE   )

title: Gallery
text: example, ’ll set simulated data reproducibility defining dataframes lanes markers. Now can call dataframes appropriate lane marker layers:
code: set.seed(123) lane_data <- tibble(   x = 0,   xend = sample(5:20, 30, replace = TRUE),   y = factor(rep(1:15, each = 2)),   colour = sample(c("red", "blue", "green", "yellow", "purple"), 30, replace = TRUE) )  set.seed(123) marker_data <- tibble(   x = sample(5:20, 30, replace = TRUE),   y = factor(rep(1:15, each = 2)),   label = sample(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"), 30, replace = TRUE),   glyph = NA ) |>   mutate(     glyph = dplyr::case_when(       label == "A" ~ "😊",       label == "B" ~ "🎉",       label == "C" ~ "✅",       label == "D" ~ "💥",       label == "E" ~ "✨",       .default = NA     )   )  # The marker scale takes one style per category, not one style per event row. emoji_styles <- marker_data |>   distinct(label, glyph) ggplot() +   geom_swim_lane(     data = lane_data,     aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, colour = colour),     linewidth = 3   ) +   geom_swim_marker(     data = marker_data,     aes(x = x, y = y, marker = label),     size = 8   ) +   scale_colour_brewer(name = "Lanes", palette = "Set1") +   with(     emoji_styles,     scale_marker_discrete(glyphs = glyph, limits = label, name = "Markers")   ) +   labs(     title = "Sample Swimmer Plot",     x = "Time", y = "Record ID"   ) +   theme_ggswim()

text: example replaces marker glyphs calls fontawesome() icons first loading fonts load_fonts(). first call load_fonts() may require internet access ggswim retrieves font files GitHub repository. Subsequent calls reuse readable cached files can work offline; missing unreadable files downloaded . glyph value Unicode text returned fontawesome(), family must match font collection supplies glyph. load_fonts() registers font families plotting; check exported image PDF well -screen preview font availability can differ graphics device.  sure specify appropriate family argument geom_swim_marker(). FontAwesome following available: “FontAwesome-Solid” “FontAwesome-Regular” “FontAwesome-Brands” can use search_fontawesome() check icons available use. ggswim supports FontAwesome free icons open source license.
code: # Load fonts from the ggswim GitHub repository load_fonts(verbose = FALSE)  marker_data <- marker_data |>   mutate(     glyph = dplyr::case_when(       label == "A" ~ fontawesome("fa-car"),       label == "B" ~ fontawesome("fa-check"),       label == "C" ~ fontawesome("fa-user"),       label == "D" ~ fontawesome("fa-cat"),       label == "E" ~ fontawesome("fa-dog"),       .default = NA     )   )  fontawesome_styles <- marker_data |>   distinct(label, glyph)  ggplot() +   geom_swim_lane(     data = lane_data,     aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, colour = colour),     linewidth = 3   ) +   geom_swim_marker(     data = marker_data,     aes(x = x, y = y, marker = label),     size = 8, family = "FontAwesome-Solid"   ) +   scale_colour_brewer(name = "Lanes", palette = "Set1") +   with(     fontawesome_styles,     scale_marker_discrete(glyphs = glyph, limits = label, name = "Markers")   ) +   labs(     title = "Sample Swimmer Plot",     x = "Time", y = "Record ID"   ) +   theme_ggswim()

code: library(ggswim) library(ggplot2)  small_lanes <- data.frame(   id = factor(c("A", "B"), levels = c("B", "A")),   cohort = c("Control", "Treatment"),   start = c(0, 0), end = c(6, 5) ) small_events <- data.frame(   id = factor(c("A", "B"), levels = c("B", "A")),   cohort = c("Control", "Treatment"),   time = c(3, 2), event = c("Response", "Response") )  small_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() +   geom_swim_lane(     data = small_lanes,     mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = start, xend = end, y = id)   ) +   geom_swim_marker(     data = small_events,     mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = id, marker = event),     size = 5   ) +   scale_marker_discrete(     glyphs = "+", colours = "steelblue", limits = "Response"   )  small_plot small_plot + ggplot2::facet_wrap(~cohort)

title: Getting Started with ggswim
text: Let’s get started building swimmer plot! README, using ggswim’s internal datasets: patient_data, infusion_events, end_study_events. Let’s start observing patient_data’s structure: patient_data contains long dataset patient IDs (pt_id) can repeated. rows differentiated disease_assessment values combined corresponding start end times, measured months. Together, rows detail clinical trial timelines patient. CR = “Complete Response” CRi = “Complete Response Incomplete Blood Count Recovery” RD = “Relapsed Disease” Now, let’s make plot using ggplot() first layer geom_swim_lane():  patient timelines split disease assessment intervals. geom_swim_lane() work setting geom_segment() readying plot layers additional ggswim-specific features “markers” mentioned earlier. ’s worth noting geom_swim_lane() thin wrapper around geom_segment() supports functionality apart yend since swimmer plots tend horizontal.
code: #> # A tibble: 75 × 4 #>    pt_id disease_assessment       start_time end_time #>    <chr> <chr>                         <dbl>    <dbl> #>  1 01    CR/CRi + B Cell Recovery       -2.8      0   #>  2 01    RD                              0        0.9 #>  3 01    CR/CRi + B Cell Aplasia         0.9      0   #>  4 01    CR/CRi + B Cell Aplasia         0        1.8 #>  5 01    CR/CRi + B Cell Recovery        1.8      2   #>  6 02    RD                             -2.8      0   #>  7 02    CRi                             0        0.2 #>  8 03    CR/CRi + B Cell Recovery       -2.4      0   #>  9 03    CR/CRi + B Cell Recovery        0        0.9 #> 10 03    CR/CRi + B Cell Aplasia         0.9      2.8 #> # ℹ 65 more rows library(ggplot2)  p <- ggplot() +   geom_swim_lane(     data = patient_data,     mapping = aes(       x = start_time,       xend = end_time,       y = pt_id,       color = disease_assessment     ),     linewidth = 3   )  p

title: Create swimmer plots with ggswim
text: Prepare included datasets, combine lanes, arrows, markers single ggplot. layer can use data sharing axes. Expand setup block run plot code; creates all_events arrow_data, plot needs.
code: library(ggswim) library(ggplot2)  all_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(infusion_events, end_study_events)  # Add arrows only for patients without an end-of-study event. arrow_data <- patient_data |>   dplyr::left_join(     dplyr::select(end_study_events, pt_id, label),     by = "pt_id"   ) |>   dplyr::select(pt_id, end_time, label) |>   dplyr::filter(.by = pt_id, end_time == max(end_time)) |>   dplyr::filter(is.na(label)) |>   dplyr::distinct() ggplot() +   geom_swim_lane(     data = patient_data,     aes(x = start_time, xend = end_time, y = pt_id,         colour = disease_assessment)   ) +   geom_swim_arrow(     data = arrow_data,     aes(xend = end_time, y = pt_id),     arrow_head_length = grid::unit(0.15, "inches")   ) +   geom_swim_marker(     data = all_events,     aes(x = time_from_initial_infusion, y = pt_id, marker = label),     size = 4   ) +   scale_colour_brewer(name = "Disease assessment", palette = "Set1") +   scale_marker_discrete(     # Match styles to event categories in the order given by limits.     glyphs = c("⬤", "⬤", "⚠️", "❌", "✅"),     colours = c("#ffde00", "#ed207f", NA, NA, NA),     limits = c("First Reinfusion", "Second Reinfusion",                "Other End Study Reason", "Deceased",                "Completed Study Follow-Up"),     name = "Study events"   ) +   labs(     title = "Disease assessments and reinfusions over time",     x = "Time since initial infusion (months)", y = "Patient ID"   ) +   theme_ggswim()

code: # Subjects without an end-study event receive continuation arrows. arrow_data <- patient_data |>   dplyr::left_join(     end_study_events |>       dplyr::select(pt_id, label),     by = "pt_id"   ) |>   dplyr::select(pt_id, start_time, end_time, label) |>   dplyr::filter(.by = pt_id, end_time == max(end_time)) |>   dplyr::filter(is.na(label)) |>   unique()  # Parameter-driven arrow styling ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_swim_arrow(   data = arrow_data,   mapping = aes(xend = end_time, y = pt_id),   linewidth = 0.1,   arrow_neck_length = 5,   arrow_head_length = grid::unit(0.25, "inches"),   arrow_colour = "slateblue",   arrow_fill = "cyan",   arrow_type = "closed" )   # Mapped start and end positions ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_swim_arrow(   data = arrow_data,   mapping = aes(x = start_time, xend = end_time, y = pt_id),   linewidth = 0.1,   arrow_head_length = grid::unit(0.25, "inches"),   arrow_colour = "slateblue",   arrow_fill = "cyan",   arrow_type = "closed" )   # Scale-driven arrow styling with a separate legend entry ggplot2::ggplot() +   geom_swim_arrow(     data = arrow_data,     mapping = ggplot2::aes(       xend = end_time,       y = pt_id,       arrow = "Continuation"     ),     linewidth = 0.1,     arrow_neck_length = 5,     arrow_head_length = grid::unit(0.25, "inches"),     show.legend = c(arrow = TRUE)   ) +   scale_arrow_discrete(     limits = "Continuation",     colours = "slateblue",     fills = "cyan",     types = "closed",     name = NULL   )
